findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag and always returns false
findings.body: The function computes `enabled` from the feature flag but then returns `false` on both branches, so the flag has no effect. Enabling `FlagSqlExpressions` cannot re-enable SQL expressions. This is probably intended as a hard kill switch, but the code reads as if the flag is honored and is misleading. Replace it with an explicit disabled path (or a comment stating the feature is unconditionally off) and remove the dead flag lookup. The `if enabled` check at line 130 also becomes dead logic.

findings.title: Error message says 'not implemented' for a feature that is disabled
findings.body: The user-facing error `sqlExpressions is not implemented` is misleading: SQL expressions are implemented but disabled for security reasons. Users and support staff will be confused about why a previously working query now fails. The message should say the feature is disabled.

findings.title: Stubbed DB methods break existing SQL command and parser behavior without updated tests
findings.body: All DB methods now return 'not implemented', so `sql.TablesList` always errors, and `NewSQLCommand`, `SQLCommand.Execute`, and the SQL parsing tests that depend on table extraction will fail. The PR adds no tests for the disabled path, and it does not update or remove the existing SQL tests. Either remove or skip those tests explicitly, or add tests that assert the disabled behavior.

findings.title: Unused stub DB path remains reachable from SQLCommand execution
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand` and `Execute` construct commands directly through `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` without going through the reader gate in `reader.go`. The gate is therefore the only protection, and a future caller that uses `NewSQLCommand` directly would bypass the disable check. Put the disable check in `NewSQLCommand` or in the stub layer so it cannot be bypassed.

findings.title: Variable name `duckDB` no longer refers to DuckDB
findings.body: After the change `duckDB` holds the stub `*DB`, which has no DuckDB backing. The name is misleading to future readers, and the `TablesList` comment still implies DuckDB-based parsing. Rename the variable and update the comment.
